```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "600px"
)

# --- CRAN Protection-----------
has_internet <- function() {
  tryCatch({
    response <- httr::GET(
      "https://api.minka-sdg.org/v1/observations",
      query = list(per_page = 1),
      httr::timeout(5)
    )
    !httr::http_error(response)
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}

is_cran_check <- identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "") || !has_internet()

if (is_cran_check) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
}

# Library protection
has <- function(p) requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)

# Only loads if is installed
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  if (has("dplyr")) library(dplyr)
  if (has("tibble")) library(tibble)
  if (has("rminka")) library(rminka)
  if (has("sf")) library(sf)
  if (has("leaflet")) library(leaflet)
  if (has("htmltools")) library(htmltools)
  if (has("purrr")) library(purrr)
  if (has("ggplot2")) library(ggplot2)
  if (has("magick")) library(magick)
})

cached_obs <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "vignette_observations.csv", package = "rminka"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
cached_obs$observed_on <- as.Date(cached_obs$observed_on)
```

This document introduces you to rminka basic set of tools, and shows you how to 
apply them to obtain your desired information.
Once you’ve installed, read vignette("rminka") to learn more.


### <u>- Project Queries </u>

Project-related functions will be illustrated using the Biomarató Tarragona
2025 project.

### ● `mnk_proj_byname()`

Initially, only the project name is known, so search for its ID with
`mnk_proj_byname()`. Here we use the query "biomarato 2025".

```{r project1, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_names <- mnk_proj_byname("biomarato 2025")

prj_names 

# For this example 

prj_names[,c(1:2)]

```
### ● `mnk_proj_info()`
 
Once the project ID is known, retrieve its details with `mnk_proj_info()`.
The Biomarató Tarragona 2025 project has ID 419.

```{r project_info, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_info <- mnk_proj_info(419)

prj_info

```
### ● `mnk_proj_user()`

Retrieve users subscribed to a project with `mnk_proj_user()` and its ID.

```{r project_info_user, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_user <- mnk_proj_user(419)

prj_user

```
Note: To retrieve all project participants, including users who are not
subscribed, download observations with `mnk_proj_obs()` and extract unique
`user_login` values. Each observation includes the observer's login.

To list participants who contributed observations in a particular month,
download that month's observations and extract unique logins. The example
below does this for May 2025:

```{r project_info_user2, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
# 1. Download all observations for the project in may 2025

obs_2025 <- mnk_proj_obs(
  419, year = 2025, month = 5, quiet = TRUE
)

# 2. Extract the unique participants

participants_may_2025 <- obs_2025 %>%
  distinct(user_login) %>%
  arrange(user_login)

participants_may_2025

```


### ● `mnk_proj_obs()`

Returns observations for a project in a selected year and, optionally, month.
For project 419, the full year 2025 is retrieved with
`mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025)`, or May with
`mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025, month = 5)`.

```{r project_obs_proj, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_obs <- mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025, month = 5)

prj_obs[2:14]

```


### <u>- User Queries</u>  

User-related functions will be illustrated using the user Xavier Salvador.
  
### ● `mnk_user_byname()`
 
Initially, only an approximate name is known, so search for the corresponding
login. Here, the query "xavi" returns possible logins; select Xavier Salvador
from the results.

```{r user_name, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_name <- mnk_user_byname("xavi")

user_name

```


### ● `mnk_user_info()`
 
Once the user ID is known, retrieve detailed information with
`mnk_user_info()`. Xavier Salvador (login "xasalva") has user ID 4.
   
```{r user_info, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_info <- mnk_user_info(4)

user_info

```


### ● `mnk_user_proj()`
 
`mnk_user_proj()` returns projects to which a user is subscribed. For Xavier
Salvador (user ID 4), use `mnk_user_proj(4)`.

Note: Projects where a user has contributed observations but is not formally
subscribed cannot be retrieved directly in R.
 
```{r user_project, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_project <- mnk_user_proj(4)

user_project

```


### ● `mnk_user_obs()`
 
Returns observations for a user in a selected year and, optionally, month.
For Xavier Salvador (user ID 4), retrieve observations for all of 2025 with
`mnk_user_obs(4, year = 2025)`, or for August with
`mnk_user_obs(4, year = 2025, month = 8)`.

```{r user_obs, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_obs <- mnk_user_obs(user_id = 4, year = 2025, month = 8)

user_obs

```


### <u>- Place Queries</u>

Place-related functions will be illustrated using the place  Piscines del Fòrum
 
### ● `mnk_place_byname()`
 
Initially, only an approximate place name is known, so search for its ID.
The query "forum" returns possible places. The place used below is "Piscines
del Fòrum" (ID 253); try different search terms if needed.

```{r place_name, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
places <- mnk_place_byname("Forum")

places[,1:6]

```

### ● `mnk_place_sf()`
 
Returns the `sf` geometry for a place. For Piscines del Fòrum, retrieve the
geometry with `mnk_place_sf(253)`.

The example maps the geometry with `leaflet` using the default WGS 84
(EPSG:4326) coordinates. The returned `sf` object includes the place name.

```{r place_sf, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
# 1. Downloading the geometry 

places_forum <- mnk_place_sf(253)

# 2. Drawing the map

 forum_sf <-leaflet(places_forum) %>%
                addProviderTiles("OpenStreetMap", group = "OSM") %>%
                addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satélite") %>%
                addPolygons(
                  color = "#2c4fb8",
                  weight = 2,
                  opacity = 1,
                  fillOpacity = 0.4,
                  label = ~name, # information added from previous function
                  highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
                    weight = 3, bringToFront = TRUE
                  )
                ) %>%
                addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satélite", "OSM"))
 forum_sf

```

### ● `mnk_place_obs()`

Returns observations recorded within a place for a selected year and,
optionally, month or day. The result is a data frame without geometry.
For Piscines del Fòrum, retrieve February 2025 observations with
`mnk_place_obs(place_id = 253, year = 2025, month = 2)`.

Convert the result to an `sf` object with `mnk_obs_sf()` and map the points
with `leaflet`.

```{r places_obs, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
obs_place <- mnk_place_obs(place_id = 253, year = 2025, month = 2, quiet = TRUE)

obs_place

# Use the packaged sample if the live query returns no observations.
if (nrow(obs_place) == 0) {
  obs_place <- subset(cached_obs, taxon_name %in% c(
    "Diplodus sargus", "Parablennius pilicornis"
  ))
}

# Convert the data frame to an sf object for mapping.
obs_sf <- mnk_obs_sf(obs_place, "id", "taxon_name", "observed_on",
                     "uri", "user_login")

# Prepare text for the marker popup.

popup_final <- paste0(
  "ID: ", obs_sf$id, "<br>",
  "Species: ", obs_sf$taxon_name, "<br>",
  "Observer: ", obs_sf$user_login, "<br>",
  "Date: ", obs_sf$observed_on
)

# Only the observations:

leaflet(obs_sf) %>%
                addProviderTiles("OpenStreetMap", group = "OSM") %>%
                addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satélite") %>%
                addMarkers(lng = ~longitude,
                           lat = ~latitude,
                           popup = popup_final) %>%
                addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satélite", "OSM"))

#  Observations plus place maping

 forum_sf %>%
  addMarkers(data = obs_sf, popup = ~popup_final)

```

### <u>- Observation Queries</u>

### ● `mnk_obs_id()`
 
Retrieves the full record for a known Minka observation ID, including its
taxonomic, location, and identification details.

```{r obs_id}
# Retrieve the observation with ID 553028.
obs_id <- mnk_obs_id(id = 553028)

obs_id

```

### ● `mnk_obs()`
 
This is the core function of the package. It supports searches by project,
user, place, date, taxon, or geographic area. Two notes apply to
`mnk_obs()` calls:

When a query runs, a message reports the number of matching observations.
By default, at most 10,000 records are downloaded. Set
`limit_download = FALSE` to retrieve all matching records.

To retrieve only validated records, use `quality = "research"`. Previous
examples covered project, user, and place searches. The following examples
show taxon and bounding-box searches.

a) <u>Taxon search</u>. The following examples search for the genus Raja in
2025 and the species Raja brachyura in 2023.

```{r obs}
# Suppress progress messages with `quiet = TRUE`.

# Get 2025 Raja observations for Xavier Salvador (user ID 4).

obs <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Raja", year = 2025, user_id = 4,
  quiet = TRUE, quality = "research"
)

obs # show full dataframe

# Get 2023 Raja brachyura observations for Xavier Salvador (user ID 4).

obs_brachyura <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Raja brachyura", year = 2023, user_id = 4,
  quiet = TRUE, quality = "research"
)

obs_brachyura[, intersect(
  c("id", "observed_on", "latitude", "longitude", "taxon_name", "user_login"),
  names(obs_brachyura)
), drop = FALSE]

```
Observation results include medium- and original-resolution photo URLs when
photos are available.

```{r brachyura-pic, out.width='85%', fig.alt="Raja undulata"}
# Get 2022 Raja undulata observations for Xavier Salvador (user ID 4).

obs_undulata <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Raja undulata", year = 2022, user_id = 4,
  quiet = TRUE, quality = "research"
)

# Display the photo URL when the query returns an observation with a photo.
if (nrow(obs_undulata) > 0 &&
    "url_picture_med" %in% names(obs_undulata) &&
    !is.na(obs_undulata$url_picture_med[1])) {
  obs_undulata$url_picture_med[1]
} else {
  message("No observation photo is available for this query.")
}

```

b) <u>Bounding-box search</u>. Retrieve observations within a rectangle by
supplying its southwest and northeast corners. The following example searches
around Platja de Sant Sebastià in Barcelona with `mnk_obs()`.

```{r obs_1}

# Read the packaged study-area shapefile.

shp_path <- system.file("extdata", "espigo_w.shp", package = "rminka")

espigo <- sf::st_read(shp_path, quiet = TRUE)

# Ensure WGS 84 coordinates for web maps.

bounds <- st_transform(espigo, 4326)

```
Alternatively, define the area with a vector of coordinates for its corners:

`bounds <- c(ymax, xmax, ymin, xmin)`

Applied to the Espigo del W example, this would be:

`bounds <- c(41.371239, 2.193971, 41.368182, 2.189147)`

The map below displays both points with the Espigó del W study area to
illustrate the `bounds` parameter.

```{r bounds}
#Pmin
xmin <- 2.189147
ymin <- 41.368182

#Pmax
xmax <- 2.193971
ymax <- 41.371239

pts <- data.frame(
  id = c("Pmin", "Pmax"),
  lng = c(xmin, xmax),
  lat = c(ymin, ymax)
)

# Create an interactive map of the study area and its corner points.

bound <- leaflet() %>%
                addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satélite") %>%
                addProviderTiles("OpenStreetMap", group = "OSM") %>%
                addCircleMarkers(             
                         data = pts,
                          radius = 20,
                          color = "cyan",
                          weight = 2,
                          fillOpacity = 0.7,
                          label = ~id,
                          popup = ~paste0("<b>", id, "</b><br>",
                                          "lon: ", round(lng, 6), "<br>",
                                          "lat: ", round(lat, 6))) %>%
                addPolygons(data =    bounds,
                          color = "#2c4fb8",
                          weight = 2,
                          opacity = 1,
                          fillOpacity = 0.4,
                          label = "Bound Espigo W",
                          popup = "Bound Espigo W",
                          highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
                            weight = 3, bringToFront = TRUE
                          )) %>%
                addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satélite", "OSM"))

bound  # display map in document

# Obtain observations within the study area.

obs_torpedo_bounds <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Torpedo", year = 2024, bounds = bounds,
  quality = "research", quiet = TRUE
)

obs_torpedo_bounds

# Use packaged sample observations if the live query returns no results.
obs_torpedo_example <- obs_torpedo_bounds
if (nrow(obs_torpedo_example) == 0) {
  obs_torpedo_example <- subset(
    cached_obs, taxon_name == "Torpedo torpedo"
  )
}

# Convert the data frame to an sf object and select fields for the map popup.

# Keep observation details for the map popup.
obs_bounds_sf <- mnk_obs_sf(
  obs_torpedo_example, "id", "taxon_name", "observed_on",
  "uri", "user_login", "quality_grade"
)

# Preparing the obtained data for later display in the marker popup

popup_final_torpedo <- paste0(
  "ID: ", obs_bounds_sf$id, "<br>",
  "Species: ", obs_bounds_sf$taxon_name, "<br>",
  "Observer: ", obs_bounds_sf$user_login, "<br>",
  "Date: ", obs_bounds_sf$observed_on
)

# Display the observations on the map.

bound %>%
  addMarkers(data = obs_bounds_sf, popup = ~popup_final_torpedo)

```


### ● `mnk_obs_byday()`
 
Works like `mnk_obs()` but uses an explicit date interval. The interval is
inclusive and is defined by:

- `d1`: Start date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format
- `d2`: End date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format

```{r obs_byday}
# Retrieve research-grade Raja undulata observations from January to May 2024.

obs_undulata_2024 <- mnk_obs_byday(
  taxon_name = "Raja undulata",
  d1 = "2024-01-01",
  d2 = "2024-05-25",
  quiet = TRUE,
  quality = "research"
)

obs_undulata_2024

```

### <u>- Auxiliary functions</u>

The first two examples use the *Torpedo torpedo* observations from the
Espigó del W study area above. The remaining examples use other data.

### ● `mnk_obs_sf()`

This function converts an observation data frame into an `sf` point layer.
It uses the latitude and longitude columns returned by `mnk_obs()` and other
observation functions. The default CRS is EPSG:4326 (WGS 84); set `crs` to
use another coordinate system. The example below uses *Torpedo torpedo*
observations from the Espigó del W study area.

```{r sf_obs,message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Convert the observations to a projected sf layer.
obs_utm <- mnk_obs_sf(
  obs_torpedo_example, id, taxon_name, observed_on, user_login,
  quality_grade, uri, crs = 25831
)

# The function retains the selected attributes and adds the geometry.

# `crs = 25831` requests ETRS89 / UTM zone 31N, a projected CRS useful
# for distance calculations and local Catalan cartography.


# Leaflet uses Web Mercator by default. To map UTM data, change the base CRS.

crs25831 <- leafletCRS(
  crsClass = "L.Proj.CRS",
  code = "EPSG:25831",
  proj4def = "+proj=utm +zone=31 +ellps=GRS80 +units=m +no_defs",
  resolutions = c(
    8192, 4096, 2048, 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64,
    32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, 0.5
  ),
  origin = c(0, 9000000)
)

# This map uses the ICGC WMS because standard OSM tiles do not use this CRS.

leaflet(options = leafletOptions(crs25831, minZoom = 0, maxZoom = 14)) %>%
  
      addWMSTiles(
        "https://geoserveis.icgc.cat/servei/catalunya/mapa-base/wms",
        layers = "orto",
        options = WMSTileOptions(format = "image/png", 
          transparent = TRUE, version = "1.3.0"
        )
      ) %>%
    
# Display observation details in the map popup.
      addCircleMarkers(
        data = obs_utm,
        radius = 6,
        color = "red",
        fillOpacity = 0.9,
        popup = paste0(
          "ID: ", obs_utm$id, "<br>",
          "Species: ", obs_utm$taxon_name, "<br>",
          "Observer: ", obs_utm$user_login, "<br>",
          "Quality: ", obs_utm$quality_grade, "<br>",
          "Date: ", obs_utm$observed_on
        )
      )
```

### ● `export_mnk_qgis()`

This function writes `sf` objects to a GeoPackage (`.gpkg`), creating one
layer per object. It supports GIS workflows such as QGIS by validating
geometries, dropping Z/M dimensions, removing unsupported list-columns,
and transforming features to the target CRS.

We will apply it to the observation layer created above.

```{r export_mnk}
output_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".gpkg")
export_mnk_qgis(observations = obs_utm, file = output_file)
unlink(output_file)

# The output path is temporary, so the example does not create a file in the
# package source directory.
#
# Multiple named sf objects can also be exported as separate GeoPackage layers:

# * places_forum: a polygon defining the Forum pools area, saved as layer "zone"

# * obs_sf: point observations from the Forum pools, saved as layer
#   "observations"
# Both layers can be written to the same GeoPackage file.

```
### ● `get_wrm_tax()`

This function retrieves taxonomic information from the
[World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS)](https://www.marinespecies.org/)
for a scientific name.
The examples show how to retrieve taxonomy for a single species and how to
combine taxonomic information with observations returned by an observation
function. The WoRMS response includes habitat flags, such as marine,
brackish-water, freshwater, and terrestrial status, as well as an extinct flag.

```{r get_taxonom_mnk}
# Retrieve taxonomy for a single species

get_wrm_tax("Diplodus sargus")

# Retrieve taxonomy for each species in the previous observation data.

unique_taxa <- obs_place %>%
  filter(!is.na(taxon_name)) %>%
  distinct(taxon_name) %>%
  pull(taxon_name)

taxonomy_df <- map_dfr(
  setNames(unique_taxa, unique_taxa),
  ~ get_wrm_tax(.x),
  .id = "taxon_name"
)

# Join the taxonomic information to the observation data.
obs_place_tax <- obs_place %>%
  left_join(taxonomy_df, by = "taxon_name")

```

### ● `shrt_name()`

This function creates a standardized abbreviation from a scientific name.
The example uses abbreviations to plot observation frequencies from
`obs_place`.

```{r shrt_name}
# Create standardized abbreviations for scientific names.

obs_place <- obs_place %>%
  mutate(
    shrt_tax_name = map_chr(taxon_name, ~ {
      if (is.na(.x) || .x == "") NA_character_ else shrt_name(.x)
    })
  )
  
# Count observations per abbreviated species and keep the top 10.

freq_top10 <- obs_place %>%
  filter(!is.na(shrt_tax_name)) %>%          # remove missing names
  count(shrt_tax_name, name = "n_obs") %>%    # count occurrences
  slice_max(n_obs, n = 10) %>%                # keep the 10 most frequent
  arrange(n_obs)   

# Plot a horizontal bar chart of observation frequency.

ggplot(freq_top10, aes(x = n_obs, y = reorder(shrt_tax_name, n_obs))) +
        geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
        geom_text(aes(label = n_obs), hjust = -0.2, size = 2) +
        scale_x_continuous(
          expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
        ) +
        labs(
              x = "Number of observations",
              y = "Species (abbreviated)",
              title = "Observation frequency",
              subtitle = " Forum February 2025"
            ) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
